jobs.description:
About Citco

JOB DESCRIPTION

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.

About The Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Responsibilities

Your Role

You will lead the Operations data, reporting and platform agenda for Private Assets — setting requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, and delivering alongside them.
Own the Operations view of the data and reporting roadmap, including data quality, lineage, ownership and reporting capability.
Set out Operations’ requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, then deliver alongside them rather than handing over.
Lead platform enablement work — ensuring platform change is specified, tested and adopted with Operations in the room throughout.
Establish reporting standards and reusable data products rather than one-off extracts.
Provide the data and evidence base that other focus areas rely on to quantify a problem and measure a benefit.
Coordinate across Operations, IT, the Transformation Office, Tactical Operations and Data Services.
Lead and mentor focus area resources, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Report on progress, risks, dependencies and benefits realisation to the relevant leader and senior stakeholders.

Qualifications

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in private assets or a comparable financial services environment, with substantial exposure to data and platform initiatives.
Proven delivery of data, reporting or platform programmes, including requirements definition and UAT ownership.
Strong technical knowledge of private assets accounting and operations, and of the data those processes produce and consume.
Practical understanding of data models, lineage, controls and reporting architecture.
Credibility with technology partners — able to challenge a design and hold a delivery date.
Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect Of The Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

This position is not for an existing vacancy; we are building a candidate pool for future opportunities.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

Our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) team within Operations helps turn high-value opportunities into practical solutions that improve how work gets done across the business. As the Director, AI Delivery, you'll lead the end-to-end delivery of a growing portfolio of AI and Generative AI initiatives, from opportunity identification and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization. You'll lead and develop a team of data scientists while creating the structure, operating rhythm, and accountability needed to deliver consistently in a complex enterprise environment. Working closely with Operations leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll translate business problems into clear, well-scoped initiatives with measurable outcomes. You'll also manage competing priorities across the portfolio, remove barriers to progress, and help ensure solutions are successfully embedded into business workflows. Success in this role means building a delivery organization that scales effectively, delivers predictably, and creates measurable business impact.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How You'll Succeed

Lead delivery excellence - Own the end-to-end delivery of the Operations AI portfolio, from intake and prioritization through development, production, adoption, and realized value. Create clear ownership, execution discipline, and accountability across initiatives.
Build trusted business partnerships - Partner closely with Operations leaders and teams to understand business needs, identify high-value AI opportunities, and shape a sustainable pipeline of use cases with clear outcomes and success measures.
Manage the portfolio - Continuously assess and prioritize concurrent AI initiatives based on business value, feasibility, capacity, dependencies, and evolving insights. Make pragmatic decisions on scope, sequencing, resourcing, and delivery approach to maintain momentum.
Navigate enterprise delivery - Drive initiatives forward with partners across data science, engineering, technology, risk, governance, and the business. Anticipate blockers and dependencies early, and work across the organization to resolve them.
Embed solutions for impact - Ensure AI solutions don't stop at production and are effectively adopted into business workflows to achieve intended outcomes. Create transparency into delivery progress, risks, capacity, portfolio health, and business value.
Develop your team - Lead, coach, and support a team of data scientists across multiple levels of experience. Help team members build ownership, strengthen stakeholder management, and increase delivery effectiveness over time.

Who You Are

You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and leading teams responsible for delivering complex technology or AI initiatives. You create clarity and accountability while empowering talented people to take ownership of their work.
You can demonstrate experience in delivering Generative AI solutions in a business environment, portfolio delivery, and cross-functional execution across business and technology teams. It’s an asset if you also bring broader experience in artificial intelligence and machine learning delivery.
You give meaning to data. You understand enough about AI and Generative AI delivery to challenge assumptions, identify delivery risks, and work effectively with data scientists and engineers. You balance technical understanding with strong business judgment.
Your influence makes a difference. You're comfortable working directly with senior business leaders and building trusted relationships across diverse partner groups. You can challenge priorities, scope, and expectations in a constructive and effective way.
You act like an owner. You focus on business outcomes, adoption, and value realization rather than activity alone. You make thoughtful trade-offs, know when to accelerate or reshape work, and can stop initiatives that aren't delivering enough value.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

jobs.description:
Working at the City of St. Albert means joining a dedicated team that aims to deliver outstanding service to our vibrant community. We pride ourselves on employing a diverse group of employees who each bring unique skills and contribute to delivering exceptional services to our residents. We value collaboration, accountability, respect, and enjoyment in our work each day.

Job Details

Reporting to the Managing Director, Corporate and Emergency Services / Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Information Technology provides strategic and operational leadership for the City’s information technology function and the Information Technology Department.

The Director is accountable for departmental performance, people, financial and resource management, and the delivery of secure, reliable, resilient, cost-effective and continuously improving enterprise technology and information management services. They ensure that technology strategies, investments, systems, projects, and service improvements align with Council priorities, corporate objectives, operational and service delivery requirements, regulatory obligations, and governance standards. As the City’s senior advisor on technology, cybersecurity, information management and digital transformation, the Director works with City leadership to establish enterprise technology strategy, governance and priorities, manages the technology portfolio, and advises Executive Leadership and Council on significant technology opportunities, risks and decisions.

Working across the organization, the Director strengthens collaboration between IT and business areas, ensures technology services and investments deliver value, respond to business needs, manage organizational risk, enable innovation and modernization, and support effective municipal service delivery.

Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the City's Information Technology Department, ensuring secure, reliable, resilient and cost-effective technology and information management services.
Establish and lead enterprise technology, information management and digital transformation strategies, priorities and long-term plans.
Provide strategic advice to Executive Leadership and Council on technology, cybersecurity, information management, business continuity, digital transformation and emerging technologies.
Oversee the City's technology investment and project portfolio, including major technology acquisitions, implementations and modernization initiatives.
Direct departmental operations, workforce planning, budgeting, resource allocation and service delivery, while fostering a high-performing, accountable and customer-focused culture.
Build strong relationships across the organization to ensure technology services, investments and priorities align with business needs, corporate objectives and effective municipal service delivery.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, or a related discipline from a recognized post-secondary institution is required. A Master's degree is preferred.
At least 10 years of progressively senior information technology experience, managing and/or directing an IT operation, including five or more years managing a major IT operation in a municipal, public sector, or recognized consulting environment.
A Diploma in computer science, information systems, or other related discipline from a recognized post-secondary institution may be considered with 15 years of related experience.
Professional certifications in project management, organizational change management, IT governance, management consulting, or IT service management are considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience with technology governance, portfolio management, investment prioritization and major project delivery.
Broad knowledge of enterprise technology, including infrastructure, cloud services, enterprise applications, networks, cybersecurity, data and information management, service management, business continuity and disaster recovery.
Strong executive leadership skills with demonstrated ability to lead managers, professional and technical teams.

Hours of Work

This position works 40 hours per week, Monday – Friday (8:00 – 5:00) and receives 1 Earned Day Off (EDO) per month.
Benefit from flexible work hours by adjusting your start and end times by 30 or 60 minutes around our business hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Compensation

The salary ranges from $164,477.56 - $198,426.54 per year, including a comprehensive benefits package with a flexible spending account, pension plan, supplementary pension, monthly vehicle allowance and accrued paid vacation starting at 5 weeks per year.
Learn more about our benefits here: Employee Benefit Guide.

Why You Should Work With Us

This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. While most employees within the department work remotely, the Director will maintain a hybrid presence to support leadership, collaboration, and operational needs. Employees are eligible to participate in this program after 3 months of employment, subject to satisfactory performance.
You will receive a Flexible Spending Account limit at the beginning of each calendar year (permanent full time $400).
Employees can purchase an annual Recreation Access Pass for $87 + tax, granting unlimited access to Servus Credit Union Place (excluding PLAYcare and registered programs), Fountain Park Recreation Centre, and Grosvenor Outdoor Pool.
Free parking near most City worksites (ask for location specific details).

Conditions of Employment

The successful candidate will be required to provide proof of educational and professional credentials.
The successful applicant will be required to obtain a satisfactory police information check.
Please note that the presence of charges or convictions does not automatically preclude an individual from being considered for employment. All findings will be reviewed and assessed in relation to the responsibilities and requirements of the position.
A valid Alberta Class 5 Driver’s Licence and access to a personal vehicle for business use are required.

Application Information

Click 'apply' and you will be taken to the City of St. Albert Careers website www.stalbert.ca/employment.
Please upload both a cover letter and resume as part of your application. These documents must be submitted as separate attachments.

CFO – Canada

Location: Calgary, AB

Company: Hero Canada Foods Inc.

About Hero Canada Foods

Hero Canada Foods is a leading branded food company and part of the international Hero Group, headquartered in Switzerland. In Canada, Hero is known for its successful portfolio of brands including Baby Gourmet, Simply Gourmet, and Goodies. Hero Canada combines local entrepreneurial agility with the scale, expertise, and long-term perspective of an international food group and is investing in systems, processes, commercial capabilities, and organizational maturity to support profitable growth.

Role Summary

Hero Canada Foods is seeking a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead all finance activities in Canada and serve as a key member of the leadership team. Reporting to the General Manager and partnering closely with Hero Group Finance, the CFO provides strategic financial leadership while maintaining a strong connection to the commercial and operational drivers of the business.

The CFO supports the General Manager in shaping strategy, setting priorities, evaluating opportunities, and navigating day-to-day operational decisions. The role provides clear financial guidance and constructive challenges while remaining close enough to the work to turn insight into action quickly.

The CFO will actively partner with the Commercial Finance Manager on pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, forecasting, and business case development, providing both strategic guidance and direct analytical support as needed. At the same time, the CFO will lead a transactional accounting team consisting of a Senior Accountant, an Accounts Payable Accountant, and an Accounts Receivable Accountant, ensuring accurate reporting, disciplined controls, and reliable execution.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Partner to the General Manager

Act as the General Manager’s trusted finance adviser on business strategy, growth priorities, organizational choices, investments, risks, and operational trade-offs.
Provide practical, fact-based guidance on day-to-day business matters, combining strategic perspective with an understanding of operational detail.
Translate financial and commercial information into clear choices, recommendations, scenarios, and actions for the General Manager and leadership team.
Constructively challenge assumptions and help align local decisions with Hero Canada’s objectives and Hero Group expectations.
Support the development and execution of the Canadian strategy, including profitable growth, margin improvement, cash generation, and operating profit protection.

2. Hands-on Commercial Finance Leadership

Lead and actively support the Commercial Finance Manager, providing coaching, prioritization, technical guidance, and direct practical assistance.
Lead financial analysis related to pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, promotions, and margin optimization, personally reviewing and supporting detailed financial models where appropriate.
Personally review, adjust, and, where required, build or manipulate detailed Excel-based pricing and commercial models rather than operating only at review level.
Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve decision quality and visibility of margins, cost drivers, pricing impacts, working capital, and profitability.
Ensure financial analysis is commercially relevant, technically sound, timely, and converted into clear recommendations.

3. Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budgeting process, rolling forecasts, performance reviews, and longer-term financial projections.
Connect commercial assumptions, supply chain realities, operating costs, and strategic initiatives into an integrated financial plan.
Monitor business performance, identify emerging gaps and opportunities, and establish corrective measures with accountable business owners.
Prepare clear reporting and decision materials for the General Manager, Canadian leadership team, Board, and Hero Group stakeholders.
Use scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to support decisions under uncertainty.

4. Accounting, Reporting & Transactional Finance Leadership

Lead the Senior Accountant, Accounts Payable Accountant, and Accounts Receivable Accountant, establishing clear ownership, priorities, service standards, and controls.
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and year-end close and ensure timely, accurate, and transparent reporting to local management and Hero Group.
Ensure accurate accounting in accordance with applicable accounting standards and Hero Group reporting requirements.
Maintain a strong internal-control environment across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, payroll, inventory, and treasury processes.
Remain sufficiently close to transactional workflows to resolve issues, remove bottlenecks, improve quality, and provide hands-on support during peak periods or complex matters.
Drive pragmatic process improvements, automation, clear documentation, and stronger use of systems and data.

5. Cash Flow, Working Capital & Risk Management

Own cash flow planning, liquidity, and working capital performance, with focused management of receivables, payables, inventory, and operating commitments.
Identify and manage financial and operational exposures, including insurance, contracts, customer and supplier risk, and foreign exchange where relevant.
Support capital allocation, funding, and investment decisions with disciplined financial analysis and recommendations.
Serve as the primary financial steward of the Canadian business, ensuring decisions support sustainable value creation and alignment with Hero Group objectives.

6. Compliance, Tax & Governance

Ensure compliance with national, provincial, local, and Hero Group financial requirements.
Coordinate external audit, tax, payroll, benefits, legal, insurance, and advisory partners as required.
Oversee statutory filings, tax compliance, transfer pricing support, corporate governance requirements, and Group reporting obligations.
Ensure appropriate documentation, approval authorities, and segregation-of-duties or compensating controls are maintained.

7. Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build one connected finance team across commercial finance and accounting, balancing business partnership with reliable transaction processing and control.
Build finance talent and organizational capability through coaching, development planning, succession management, and cross-functional business exposure.
Develop the Commercial Finance Manager as a strong business partner while remaining available for detailed technical and modelling support.
Create a working culture that values accuracy, pace, ownership, practical problem-solving, continuous improvement, and constructive challenge.
Provide clear goals, coaching, feedback, succession planning, and development opportunities.

Team Structure

Reports to: General Manager, Hero Canada
Functional connection: Hero Group Finance
Direct leadership over: Commercial Finance Manager; Senior Accountant; Accounts Payable Accountant; Accounts Receivable Accountant

Required Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including meaningful senior finance leadership responsibility.
Experience serving as a CFO, VP Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leader within a growth-oriented, lean operating environment.
Strong commercial finance experience with demonstrated depth in pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.
Advanced Excel capability and willingness to work directly in detailed models and analyses.
Strong technical foundation in financial reporting, accounting, internal controls, cash flow, working capital, audit, tax, and compliance.
Experience leading both commercially oriented finance professionals and transactional accounting teams.
Experience in an international or cross-border business environment; CPG, food, manufacturing, distribution, or branded consumer products experience preferred.
Experience leading finance process improvements, ERP implementations, reporting enhancements, and finance transformation initiatives.

Strategic and commercial mindset
Hands-on analytical and problem-solving capability
Influence and stakeholder management
Financial stewardship and risk management
Leadership and talent development
Continuous improvement orientation
Executive communication and presentation skills
High integrity and sound judgment
Financial modelling, analytical, and technical accounting capability
